Before the Internet was an assumption that everyone had access to and could patch any game at any time, games were shipped "as is" with the assumption that the game must be playable if a single patch is never applied. Thus cartridge games will still play today just as well today as they did if their console's hardware still functions. With the advent of always on connections, authentication servers, and major parts of games never being on the client side copy of software, once the servers shut down, the game is broken. Unless a server shows up on ebay years later, or sold in bankruptcy proceedings, that server code may be lost forever, and the game play it once held is only documented in youtube videos. once youtube goes down, those videos are lost except for the few who saved a copy to their hard drives, and only so long as those drives hardware survives.

Game companies will face a very harsh lesson as their place in history books is not determined by how much money they make, not how large their peak user base was, but how well they contained their game play to survive the harshest tests of time. The lost of a user base, the loss of funding, the loss of functioning hardware to create the game play its designers achieved. so many games will be lost as the servers for playstation 3 and xbox 360 go offline, and the xbox one will fail to boot up, as will many more systems to come.

The only games to survive the server shutdowns and company bankruptcy are those which are:

  1. feature complete without any patches.

  2. does not require any external connection to function.

  3. can connect directly to another I.P. address for a multi player match (if applicable).

Companies rise and fall, games come and go, but design decisions in those games last forever.

What legacy will your games leave behind?
